transcript:
It was a tipical Tuesday morning. When I entered the class
some students were laughing and having their own tiny conversation, while others were going around
to the class to greet one another. overlapping conversation
something that I had grown used to every day
filled the room. Then I spotted my best friend, Mary. I went
to her and greeted her with a pleasant smile. We were best friends
from kindergarden, we would always hang out in my house
every friday after school. We would also share very
secrets with one another as well. Just then the teacher
walked in. Instantly everyone went back to their seat.
The movment was quick but natural; something that happened
everyday with not much thought in it. So Mary and
I settled in our seats, ready to start the lesson.

Then my teacher, Ms Tan assinged us some work
to do. Moment after I started doing my assignment,
I heard something that caught my attention.
I heard a buch of student from the tabdle beside me

talking about something very personal about me. It was also
one of the secrets that I only told Mary and not a single soul
in the class. 'How do they know? How much do they know?
What more would they know? And most importantly how would
have told them?!' All these such thought filled my mind.
Just then a thought that I would never think or poped
in my brain. 'What if Mary told them?' I thought. I was
speechless. For the whole lesson I was think how would Mary
possible betray me like that. After a while the recess
bell rang. Upon hearing that the students rushed to hand in
the paper and bolted down to the school canteen wanting
to beat the long queue line out the stalls. As I made my way
slowly down to the canteen still in disbelief of what
happen in class earlear.

When I reached the canteen I spotted Mary.

without hesitation I stomped towards her as I was raging
with anger. "Why would you do such a thing! I trusted you
to keep my secrets and you go around telling people
about it!" I shouted. She was looking so lost in my word and
looked she had absolutely no idea what I was talking which made
me even frustrated. "Oh stop pretending like you do not know
what I am talking about." I raised my voice once more.
Before she could say a word I angrily walk away.

For the whole day I avoided her, not wanting to
see her. When she kept coming up to me to explain herself,
I kept going away from her. Later the teacher
partented us together so I had not choice but to talk to her.
Then she asked if she would explain herself one more time.
I said "fine" in a stern voice while crossing my arms. Mary
said that she would never tell anyone my secret as
she knew how much it meant to me, and that another

might just hear us talking. At that second a
wave of embarrassment washed over me. I apologized sincerely to
her for accusing her unfairly and for refusing to let her
explain the problem. Although she was hurt by my
action, she eventually forgiven me

The expireants taught me that trust can easily
be damage with assumptions and impulsive actions.
From that day onwards I learned that I should not assume
something that I do not know fully about and I also learned
to stay calm and commutacat properly before jumping
to conclusion.

errors.note: Days of the week must be capitalized.
Plural subject pronoun 'their' requires plural noun 'seats'.
Plural noun required after 'a bunch of'.
First word of sentence must be capitalized.
Past tense 'walked' required to match narrative tense.
Past simple 'forgave' required instead of past participle.
Passive verb form requires past participle 'damaged'.
Plural noun required in standard expression 'jumping to conclusions'.
